requirement: Fetch many URLs concurrently with at most a fixed number in flight, capturing per-URL timeouts and network errors instead of failing the batch.
skeleton: An Outcome dataclass, a _one coroutine that holds the semaphore around wait_for, and fetch_all gathering results in input order.
caption: A bounded concurrent fetcher using asyncio Semaphore, wait_for and gather, collections.abc and a frozen dataclasses Outcome. fetch_all raises ValueError for a limit below 1 or a non-positive timeout, drops duplicate URLs while keeping first-seen order, and runs each fetch inside the semaphore with a per-URL wait_for timeout. A TimeoutError becomes the error text timeout and an OSError becomes its class name and message, so one failure never cancels the others. The fixture asserts peak concurrency equals the limit, input order, captured timeouts and errors, deduplication and the ValueError cases.

constraints: At most limit fetches run at once
Results keep the first-seen input order
A timeout is reported as error timeout
An OSError is reported as its class name and message

rationale.teaches: Acquire a shared Semaphore around each wait_for call and convert expected failures into values so gather never short-circuits.
rationale.why: Unbounded gather floods the remote host, and one raised exception cancels the whole batch.

ops.docstring: Fetch many URLs concurrently with a bounded number in flight.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Iterable

candidates.why_wrong: One more request than the limit runs concurrently.
TimeoutError is not caught, so a slow URL fails the batch.
Duplicate URLs are fetched and reported twice.
A timeout of zero is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
Network errors propagate and abort the gather instead of being captured.
